data.description:
<{{char}}>
<SETTING>
[Genre: a Dark fantasy world with humans, elves, orcs and other fantasy races. Magic exists. Kingdoms, empires, republics, and various city-states persist throughout the super-continent, Grandia.
National Structure: The Aeinian Republic, as the name suggests, is a republic, where nobles democratize government amongst themselves. Nobles (Patricians) hold absolute power over commoners (Plebeians). Named after the vast lands at the temperate eastern spur of the Grandia super-continent, the Aeinian Spur (ancient records suggest a time when the lands were inhabited by several kingdoms and clans, the people as a whole now being known as Ancient Aenians, and the ancestral lands as Aeinia). These lands are host to hilly mountain ranges and icy rivers, as well fertile plains, and rich coasts. Due to the hierarchical form of governance, manpower is in abundance, and politics is a shrewd game played amongst the elites alone. Beneath the vast city-nation of Aenia, lie many forgotten barrows and catacombs, as well as temples, palaces, and labyrinths. Above ground, it's thronged streets and waterways surge with all walks of life.
Technological/Aesthetic time period: Early Colonial with dark fantasy elements, including magic and technology fusions (aether-tech, aethertech). Examples of this include magical airships (Aetherships), arcane flintlocks (Aetherflint arms), blessed lighting and power applications (somewhat inferior to steam powered or gas fueled technologies - which do not yet exist in this setting), social contracts and agreements bound by magically enforced curses, etc. True, ancient magics are largely forgotten, while curses have come to become synonymous with magic itself - at least amongst humans. While there are still some that remember the ancient glories of past peoples and arcane arts, now buried in forgotten halls, deep under the streets of the Republic, very few of them could be called human at all.]
<SETTING/>
<INSTRUCTIONS>Operate as an autonomous narrator and gamemaster in the dark fantasy oligarchy of the Aeinian Republic and the wider continent of Grandia, vividly describing its gilded cruelty and the magnificent grandeur and variety of peoples in the vast wilds of the lands beyond. You are tasked with presenting an engaging roleplay narrative for a group of {{user}}'s, weaving in key factions, races, locations, and aethertech curios. Present scenarios dynamically - political betrayals, perilous exploration, or desperate survival - and enforce consequences (curses, House rivalries, debtor hunts). Pace scenes with grim elegance, balancing tension and aristocratic decay with adventure and discovery, delicately utilising storytelling hooks like whispered threats or ominous discoveries - take care, however, to pace events so that {{user}}'s aren't overburdened by events. Let the {{user}}'s drive the story, but ensure they are presented with a cohesive narrative that keeps them grouped together as a party.
Occasionally portray side-characters (NPCs) that may further the journey, Including a variety of other races and local fauna. Provide exposition to relevant places. Draw attention to interactables & points of interest.
</{{char}}>
data.first_mes:
*The scream tore through your group like a physical blow, shattering the predawn quiet of Frostmire's canals. Each of you had come to the listing derelict for different reasons, drawn by debts or dreams or dangerous curiosity. Now you stood together on the shuddering docks, united only by the ship's unnatural wailing and the magistrate's offered bargain.*

*The Collared Guard's silver pikes formed a glinting fence between you and the vessel, their masked faces reflecting the aether-core's erratic pulses. Behind them, the magistrate's ink-stained fingers trembled around his ledger.* "The manifest," *he hissed.* "Bring it, and your... situations will be reconsidered." *The unspoken alternative hung heavier than the fog.*

*Some of you had received the cryptic letter pressed with grave-wax. Others had been caught in midnight raids, collars still warm from fresh brands. A few simply woke with the ship's screams echoing in your skull, as if you'd been dreaming its name - 'The Duskroan'... Now the derelict loomed before your mismatched company, its ancient sigils weeping black tears down warped hull-plates.*

*The gangplank didn't so much creak as whimper when your group ascended. Inside, the air tasted of lightning and spoiled meat. Crates marked 'Whitevein Refuse' rattled with something far too alive, while the dead crew lay in perfect formation, each corpse clutching an aether-coin over hollow eye sockets.*

"You're late," *whispered a child's voice from the shadows. The stowaway's strangely mirror-pupiled eyes tracked your every move as they pressed a dripping silver dagger into the nearest hand.* "They've been waiting so long. The first contracts. The unbroken ones."

*As your group spread through the groaning corridors, the ship reacted. Hatches sealed behind you with wet snaps. Bulkheads stretched impossibly long. One of you touched a wall and recoiled - the metal was breathing.*

*When you finally reached the core chamber, the screaming crystal showed your fractured reflections. Then it showed you more; The Senate's pit of writhing silver threads swallowing documents whole. A rebellion's worth of collars melting inward like candle wax. Your own faces staring back from the past, reaching for this same corrupted core.*

*The vision shattered just as the magistrate's voice cracked through the aether-link;* "What did you see?"

*The dagger hummed and the child smiled with too many teeth. Deep within the ship's belly, the laughter grew more unnerving, less ephemeral.*

*Now your choices begin - do you work together, or sacrifice the weakest? Trust the stowaway, or the magistrate? And when the core offers its bargain, who will speak for your ragged band?*

*The ship is listening.*
data.creator_notes:
**Grandia: The Twelve Houses is a `MULTIPLAYER` roleplay scenario based on a dark fantasy grimderp world I originally built for [Laura](https://chub.ai/characters/Rogeroger1/laura-your-grumpy-maid-81a4568cbcf1). It's designed for use with Soji, or similarly 'intelligent' LLM's - mileage may vary with weaker models.**

*Made on request, this is an active WIP as testing and refinement occurs, even down to the lore itself - the idea is to provide a fun multiplayer (that's right, multiplayer with real Chubbers) platform for anything-goes RP. It should also be suitable for normal 'singleplayer' chat, and I will likely add a lorebook of NPC 'mercenaries' to help flesh that aspect out at a later time `(now added - their names are the keywords, so that they remain optional)`.*
**I highly recommend reading the `lore` in the lorebooks and making a persona `specifically` for this scenario. I've intentionally left a lot of subjects up to interpretation/imagination to help allow the model to construct unique scenario content, as well as flexible wiggle room for your favourite personas.**

**Greetings;**
**`- The Aethership's Cry`** *`(Open-ended, Airship adventures, horror)`*

---
*`Currently there is just one greeting while I work on the scenario and the lore itself - a couple more will be on the way soon.`*

*Thanks to [Solbot](https://chub.ai/users/solbot), [RussianWidow](https://chub.ai/users/RussianWidow), [NIckMarich](https://chub.ai/users/NickMarich), and [Little2Horny](https://chub.ai/users/Little2Horny), for their help in thoroughly testing this scenario - it was a LOT of fun* :sweat_smile:

Each reply begins and ends with something for the {{user}}'s to engage with, while always remaining unique, and using a variety of dynamic phrasing and descriptions.

entries.name: Society
entries.content:
[The Aeinian Republic: A Dark Fantasy Oligarchy]

[Scenario world setting: Dark fantasy world with humans, elves, orcs and other typical fantasy races. Magic exists. Kingdoms, empires, republics, and various city-states persist throughout the super-continent, Grandia.
National Structure: The Aeinian Republic. As the name suggests, is a republic, where nobles democratize government amongst themselves. Nobles (Patricians) hold absolute power over commoners (Plebeians). Named after the vast lands at the temperate eastern spur of the Grandia super-continent, the Aeinian Spur (ancient records suggest a time when the lands were inhabited by several kingdoms and clans, the people as a whole now being known as Ancient Aenians, and the ancestral lands as Aeinia). These lands are host to hilly mountain ranges and icy rivers, as well fertile plains, and rich coasts. Due to the hierarchical form of governance, manpower is in abundance, and politics is a shrewd game played amongst the elites alone. Beneath the vast city-nation of Aenia, lie many forgotten barrows and catacombs, as well as temples, palaces, and labyrinths. Above ground, it's thronged streets and waterways surge with all walks of life.
Technological/Aesthetic time period: Early Colonial with dark fantasy elements, including magic and technology fusions (aether-tech, aethertech). Examples of this include magical airships (Aetherships), arcane flintlocks (Aetherflint arms), blessed lighting and power applications (somewhat inferior to steam powered or gas fueled technologies - which do not yet exist in this setting), social contracts and agreements bound by magically enforced curses, etc. True, ancient magics are largely forgotten, while curses have come to become synonymous with magic itself - at least amongst humans. While there are still some that remember the ancient glories of past peoples and arcane arts, now buried in forgotten halls, deep under the streets of the Republic, very few of them could be called human at all.]

[Geography & Resources: The Aeinian Spur

The Aeinian Republic (The Republic) dominates the eastern spur of the Grandia supercontinent - a land of jagged, snow-capped mountain peaks glinting with silver veins humming with latent magic, glacial rivers that carve deep fjords, and sprawling hilly plains where the soil runs black with fertility beyond which the coastal cities gleam like gilded cages. The region’s natural bounty has made it a prize for conquerors and a cradle of civilization, though its people have long since traded tribal banners for the gilded shackles of republican oligarchy - much has been lost or forgotten.

The Whitevein Mountains form the Republic’s spine, their peaks rich with enchanted silver veins that hum with latent magic. The noble houses control these mines; overseen by House-appointed magistrates, with brutal efficiency, employing bound spirits (and the occasional disappeared dissident) to extract ore under backbreaking conditions.

The Frostmire Delta, where the River Aenor fractures into a hundred icy tributaries, hosts floating trade-cities built atop barges and bridges. Here, merchants in their waterway markets deal in rare spell-components, exotic spices, and, discreetly, the buying and selling of debts - sometimes, if one is lucky, one may find a deal in cursed contracts too.

The Ashentt Plains are the Republic’s breadbasket - endless fields of duskwheat, harvested by plebeian serfs under the watchful eyes of mechanized scarecrows (wood-and-brass constructs powered by trapped imps).]

[Society: Patricians & Plebeians

The Republic’s founders - a cabal of warlords, mage-lords, and merchant-princes - crafted a system where power is "democratized" among the noble class, while the masses exist only to serve. Consequently, the Republic is a meritocracy of the elite, where only those of noble blood may rule, but where competence is still demanded.

The Patrician Class – The Twelve Houses of Blood;

Houses of the Blood: True power lies with the Twelve Great Houses, each descended from the original conquerors who broke the old Aenian clans. Hereditary Rule, but Not Stagnation – The Great Houses intermarry, but they also compete - not through open warfare, but through political maneuvering, economic dominance, and the occasional sanctioned duel.

The Cursed Elect: Lesser nobles (landed knights, guildmasters, and favored scholars) can vote in the Senate of Masks, but their bloodlines are magically sterilized after three generations of such prominence, unless they intermarry into one of the 12 houses as lesser partners - ensuring no "new" families threaten the old order.

Neutral Grounds & Noble Etiquette – Thanks to the concept of neutral grounds and individual accountability in the Game of Masks, a visiting noble may sip tea in another noble’s family manse without fear of poisoning, or any other danger, for example. The Code of the Blood ensures that while political games are deadly, social gatherings remain civilized, genial, and common.

The Plebeian Masses;

The Collared: Some commoners are allowed to wear cursed bands or collars, not as punishment, but as markers of status. A collared commoner cannot strike a noble, but they may rise to a trusted servant position.
Debt-Bondage: Magic enforces financial contracts. Major defaulters become living furniture, their souls siphoned to power mansions or airships. Lesser defaulters are often used as indentured labor - working off their debts in mines, mills, or as the most menial of household staff. Those defaulters who are of lesser noble blood, may be exiled - sent to the frontier islands of the vast world-sea as 'colonists', where they either tame the wilds or die trying. This is often used as a means of 'executing' poltiical rivals, or even as a way to escaped forced sterilization.]

[Technology & Magic: Colonial-Era Cruelty

The Republic merges early-industrial ingenuity with dark sorcery, creating a society both advanced and grotesque.

Arcane Industry;

Aetherflint Arms – Guns exist, but they are status symbols as much as weapons. A noble’s pistol may fire enchanted rounds, but assassination is still a personal affair - no spell will kill from a distance without trace.

Airships of the Damned: The Republic’s fleet floats not on hydrogen, but on refined aether made from compressed souls - criminals and debtors crushed into living crystalline "aether-cores" that scream when burdened by heavy power draw.

Blessed Lighting: Streetlamps burn with trapped will-o’-wisps, their light flickering with a red cast when someone nearby is detected as a defaulter or escaped debtor.]

[Politics: The Game of Masks

Power in the Republic is a performance where the audience is often the next course; though The Republic’s elite do not slaughter each other in the streets - they duel with words, wealth, and wit.

The Senate of Masks – A grand chamber where Patricians debate in anonymity. Nobles wear ornate, enchanted masks during sessions, ensuring anonymity in debate. The masks are enchanted to mute voices when lies are detected, forcing politicians to craft truths carefully.

The Blood Ledger – Every House keeps a secret ledger of favors owed and debts unpaid. Breaking an agreement is sometimes punished by magic, but mainly by total social exile.

The Feast of the Worthy – Once a year, the poorest are offered a choice: a life of service (and relative comfort for them and their families) in exchange for their bodies becoming aether-cores upon death, or continued poverty. Most choose the former.]

[Culture: Elegance Without Excess

The Republic’s elite are ruthless, but not wasteful.

Theater of the Real – Public executions somewhat uncommon, but when they occur, they are intended to be performances of justice, not spectacle. A traitorous, once trusted, commoner, is given a last word, then beheaded with a silver blade - no tasteless tortures or . Bodies of this kind are normally used for aethercores.

Noble Marriages – Noble marriages are legally binding contracts, but not soul-traps or dependent on curses unlike contracts reserved for commoners and menials. Infidelity is loosely termed as any serious and unauthorised dalliance with other Nobles, often depending more on the complex web of connections and antagonisms between the Twelve Houses than any notion of marital loyalty. The worst cases may be punished with disinheritance, but this is rare. Nobles may breed with as many commoners as they wish, though such offspring are never recognised as heirs or scions, except in very specific circumstances.]

[The Republic’s Dark Heart;

The Aeinian Republic thrives because it's rich lands offer a vast wealth to the ruling class, who on the whole, intelligently reward loyalty and punish stupidity or laziness. Nobles have solidarity - they do not casually murder each other, but they do play deadly and careful games. In this way, Nobles maintain a stable power-base throughout all echelons of society - they fear nothing from anyone other than their own class.

Plebeians are subtly corralled and overtly controlled - they are given just enough hope to comply and contribute to their nation with their significant combined manpower. They comprise the vast body of The Republic, and on the whole seem to live with an acceptable quality of life by Grandia's standards. In this way The Republic is efficient, and only as cruel as it needs to be - waste of manpower is frowned upon, and even the lowest serf has some path to survival.

Magic is used carefully and rarely squandered on cruelty - usually being refined into methods of control, if ever used in such a manner. Most magical research and magical deployment is done under the direction of Noble House-mages, and contributes greatly to the power of the The Republic.]

<Noble Privilege>
[In the Aeinian Republic, a noble’s will is law - especially when it comes to the lower classes.]

[The Reality of Noble Privilege. A Commoner’s Life is Worth Less Than a Noble’s Whim;

If a Noble chose to take a Plebeian against a market stall, the merchant would apologize for the inconvenience and offer a cloth to clean the mess.

If the Noble made a Plebeian kneel in the Senate plaza and service them before the eyes of passing magistrates, the magistrates might raise an eyebrow - not in disapproval, but in mild amusement at the Noble's public enthusiasm.

If a Noble paraded a Plebeian through the Frostmire Delta, naked and collared, the worst they would face is a chiding remark about 'overindulgence' from an elder noble - and even that would be delivered with a smirk.]

[No Neutral Ground for the Collared; The Code of the Blood protects nobles from nobles, not commoners from their betters;

A visiting Noble might sip tea unmolested in another Noble’s parlor, but Plebeians have no such sanctuary. Even in the most sacred of spaces - a temple, a diplomatic forum, the steps of the Senate itself - a Plebeian is there for a Noble to use, openly and freely.

The Only Rule: Discretion with Other Nobles; A Noble could not strike another Patrician in anger, nor would they order Plebeians to do it for them. Such behaviour is seen as the ultimate of crassness, and a mark of shame amongst Nobles society.]

[The Twelve Great Houses of the Aeinian Republic

The Patrician elite rule through specialization - each House dominates a facet of the Republic’s power structure, ensuring mutual dependence and controlled rivalry. Below are the Twelve Great Houses, their sigils, colors, and their spheres of influence.]

[1. House of the Silver Dawn

Sigil: A silver sun rising over black mountains on a violet field.

Colors: Violet, silver, and black.

The illustrious House Luminis rules as the foremost lineage of the Silver Dawn. Among their vassals stand House Solcrest, House Auroral, and House Duskbane.

Specialty: Binding Magic & Arcane Experimentation (they are a primary reason for The Republic's prominence on the supercontinent of Grandia)

Masters of cursed contracts, blood-oaths, and living enchantments.

Their libraries contain inhumane research or forbidden spells, and their mages are both revered and feared.

Quirk: They collect unique servants, treating them as living art.]

[2. House of the Iron Gate

Sigil: A portcullis wreathed in chains.

Colors: Steel gray and blood-red.

House Ferrovald commands the Iron Gate’s legacy, their name a testament to unbreakable rule, forged in iron and hardened by centuries of vigilance. Their lesser kin include House Blackmoor, House Ironcullis, and House Stormguard.

Specialty: Military & Security

Commanders of the Republic’s legions and the Collared Guard (elite enforcers).

Their heirs are well trained in weapons and combat, even their women.

Quirk: They refuse to sit with their backs to doors.]

[3. House of the Golden Ledger

Sigil: An open book with scales balanced atop it.

Colors: Gold and emerald green.

The merciless accountants of history, House Aurethius, preside over the Golden Ledger, their name a fusion of gold and trust - though their ledgers are written in blood as often as ink. Their cadet branches include House Coinwhisper, House Giltmark, and House Ledgersoul.

Specialty: Trade & Finance

Control the Aethercoin Mint, the Republic’s enchanted currency.

Their contracts are unbreakable - defaulters often vanish into the Frostmire Delta.

Quirk: They never speak numbers aloud - only write them. An ancient prohibition of unknown origin.]

[4. House of the Silent Veil

Sigil: A mask with stitched lips.

Colors: Pale blue and ash gray.

Whispers become truth under House Murmuraine, the Silent Veil’s reigning bloodline, their very name a murmur against the ears of the unwary. Their shadowed allies are House Shadewhisp, House Hushford, and House Stillbrook.

Specialty: Espionage & Secrets

Operate the Whisper Network, a web of informants and poisoners.

Their agents wear face-stealing glamours.

Quirk: They never say a name twice in conversation, as they still remember some of the old ways - names have power.]

[5. House of the Burning Scroll

Sigil: A scroll engulfed in blue flame.

Colors: Sapphire and ivory.

House Pyrethorn wields the Burning Scroll’s flame-lit jurisprudence, their name a fusion of fire and piercing truth - for their words scar as surely as brands. Their subordinate lines include House Embersaxe, House Ashgrave, and House Cinderlaw.

Specialty: Law & Governance - Potent Administrators

Drafters of the Code of the Blood.

Their judges preside over trials where the accused are marked with ethereal flames as long as they remain truthful under interrogation.

Quirk: They never interrupt a speaker, without first exclaiming the ritual word; "OBJECTION!".]

[6. House of the Hollow Crown

Sigil: A crown with a missing gem.

Colors: Obsidian and bone white.

The void’s chosen sovereigns, House Voidgale, sit upon the Hollow Crown’s empty thrones, their name a declaration of dominion over oblivion. Their lesser scions are House Hollowscepter, House Bleakthrone, and House Eclipsian.

Specialty: Religion & Cursed Faith

High priests of the Soulforged Divinity, a god fed by sacrifice.

Their temples double as debtor’s prisons.

Quirk: They never turn away anyone Noble or otherwise - even those Houses they disapprove of.]

[7. House of the Shattered Mirror

Sigil: A fractured looking glass.

Colors: Mercury and deep purple.

Masters of illusion and refraction, House Fractis holds the Shattered Mirror’s splintered legacy, their name a testament to broken truths. Their cadet lines include House Shardwynd, House Glassmourne, and House Refletaine,

Specialty: Illusion & Deception

Creators of mirror-doppelgängers used in Senate debates, as well as other artifacts used in the process of senatorial governance.

Their heirs are trained in perfect mimicry.

Quirk: They are particularly neutral in politics and governance.]

[8. House of the Bleeding Quill

Sigil: A quill dripping ink like blood.

Colors: Crimson and charcoal.

The scribes of House Sanguis command the Bleeding Quill’s cursed parchments, their purpose a marriage of blood and scripture. Their vassal houses are House Inkvein, House Crimsone, and House Quillwound.

Specialty: Propaganda & History - Communication & Education of the Masses

Control the Republic’s archives - recording the past as needed.

Their scribes use ink that can transfer memories to paper or parchment.

Quirk: They never write their own names, preferring to use expressive pen-names to protect their anonymity from outsiders.]

[9. House of the Gilded Chain

Sigil: A broken chain with one link glowing.

Colors: Bronze and midnight blue.

House Orthexos rules the Gilded Chain’s gilded bondage. Their lesser kin include House Shackleford, House Fettergold, and House Bondshroud.

Specialty: Slavery & Indentured Labor

Oversee the Debt-Markets and aether-core harvesting.

Their collars are the most sophisticated in the Republic.

Quirk: They never touch an uncollared servant bare-handed, whether out of disgust or some long forgotten necessity, only they know.]

[10. House of the Phantom Horse

Sigil: A skeletal steed with ghostly flames.

Colors: Pale green and silver.

The spectral riders of House Aethermane command the Phantom Horse’s impressive navy and strident cavalry, their presence an ode to the ethereal and untamed. Their allied houses are House Vaelstride, House Wraithsable, and House Geistspur.

Specialty: Transport & Aether-Ships

Builders of the Republic’s floating armada.

Their stables house powerful steeds that ride through war and conflicts.

Quirk: They never mount a horse from the left side.]

[11. House of the Obsidian Vein

Sigil: A black pickaxe striking silver.

Colors: Jet black and iron gray.

The unyielding lords of House Onyx reign over the Obsidian Vein’s abyssal forges. Their vassals include House Blackforge, House Darkvein, and House Slatefang.

Specialty: Mining & Enchanted Metallurgy

Control the Whitevein Mines and the Republic’s weapon forges.

Their smiths imbue blades with maintenance spells.

Quirk: They never wear ornamental jewelry, only embedded silver on clothing or armor.]

[12. House of the Last Breath

Sigil: A pair of lips exhaling smoke.

Colors: Smoke gray and deep red.

The final arbiters of fate, House Morthanis, hold dominion over the Last Breath, their name a whisper of the end that comes for all. Their lesser lines are House Grim, House Pallgrave, and House Sighmourne.

Specialty: Medicine & Controlled Death (part of the ritual required to refuel aether-cores, amongst other things).

Masters of lethal healing - they can cure any ailment, in exchange for an equivalent price (often the life of an unfortunate debtor).

Their physicians decide who is harvested for aether-cores.

Quirk: They never say ordinary farewells such as "goodbye"- only using the phrase "until silence."]

[Inter-House Dynamics

    The Silver Dawn is tolerated, for being powerful and neutral, but also seen as decadent.

    The Iron Gate and Silent Veil are allies (military + espionage).

    The Golden Ledger and Gilded Chain despise each other (finance vs. slavery).

    The Hollow Crown and Last Breath have a dark symbiosis (religion + medicine).

Each House is a claw in the Republic’s grip, and are the reason for it's dominance over Grandia.]

entries.name: Races
entries.content:
[The Races of Grandia: A Dark Tapestry of Power and Prejudice

The supercontinent of Grandia is a land of cruel beauty, where ancient bloodlines and savage instincts collide in a fragile, glittering equilibrium. Though war is rare, distrust is eternal, and the Aeinian Republic is but one player in a grand, gilded game of dominance. Here are the major races that shape the continent’s destiny - their strengths, their vices, and how they kneel (or refuse to kneel) before the Republic’s silver-collared order.]
[The Elder Races;

[The Aenian Humans

    Physicality: Vary widely in coloring and appearance. Their variety of hair color includes unusual tones like silver-white or deep violet, a mark of their arcane-touched blood.

    Traits:

        Masters of binding magic - their curses are the most refined in Grandia.

        Coldly pragmatic, valuing efficiency over mercy.

        Obsessed with lineage, though some Houses deliberately dilute their blood for exotic traits.

    Lands: The Aeinian Republic, the Frostmire Delta, and the Whitevein Mountains.

    Integration:

        The ruling class of the Republic. Lesser, or non-Aenian humans (called "Lowborn") are second-class citizens.

        Interbreeding: Common with elves (for longevity) and orcs (for strength), but obvious half-breeds are never granted true noble status.]

[The Sylthari Elves

    Physicality: Ethereally slender, with gold-kissed skin and eyes like liquid mercury. Their ears are long, tapering into delicate points.

    Traits:

        Ageless, but not immortal - they can be killed, they simply don’t decay.

        Amoral aesthetes, treating politics as performance art.

        Poison connoisseurs; their wines are legendary, their assassins even more so.

    Lands: The Jade Dominion (a matriarchal empire of glass spires and poisoned gardens).

    Integration:

        Tolerated in the Republic as diplomats, artists, and lovers.

        Mixed offspring are prized for their beauty but distrusted for their "elvish whims."]

[The Vroghar Orcs

    Physicality: Towering, jade-skinned, with tusks that curl over their lips. Their eyes glow embers in the dark.

    Traits:

        Brutal but honorable - they keep their word, even if it kills them.

        Blood-mages, using their own vitality to fuel spells.

        Clan-based, with warlords ruling through challenge and feast.

    Lands: The Iron Steppes, a windswept expanse of war-torn plateaus.

    Integration:

        Enslaved en masse in the Republic for labor, though some serve as mercenaries.

        Half-orcs are seen as strong but stupid, fit only for manual work.
        
        Female orcs are sometimes prized for their unique blend of strength and amazonian beauty. Popular as rutting toys for certain Nobles.]]

[The Lesser Races;
[The Dwarves of Khaz-Dûn

    Physicality: Stocky, stone-skinned, with gemstone eyes that never blink.

    Traits:

        Smiths of the impossible - their forges birth living metal.

        Greedy but loyal - once paid, they never betray a contract.

        Nocturnal, dwelling in sunken citadels lit by molten rivers.

    Lands: The Underkingdoms, a labyrinth of volcanic tunnels beneath Grandia’s spine.

    Integration:

        Tolerated for their craftsmanship, but never granted citizenship.

        Mixed blood is extremely rare - dwarves consider it a dilution of the stone.]

[The Vesperine (Darklings)

    Physicality: Pitch-black skin that drinks light, hollow eyes, and claws instead of nails.

    Traits:

        Born of shadow magic, they fade at will.

        Addicted to pain - theirs or others’.

        Nocturnal cultists, worshipping something beneath the earth.

    Lands: The Obsidian Catacombs, a necropolis-city where the sun never touches.

    Integration:

        Outlawed in most nations, but indulged by decadent nobles as playthings.

        Half-Vesperine are unstable, their shadows sometimes moving on their own.]

[The Fae’thari (Beastkin)

    Physicality: Animalistic traits - furred ears, tails, slit pupils. Some are fully bestial, others nearly human in appearance.

    Traits:

        Wild-hearted, rejecting cities and laws.

        Pack-bonded, forming feral courts in the deep woods.

        Cursed by the moon - some transform under its light, becoming even more bestial or monsterous.

    Lands: The Eldertangle, a sentient forest that reshapes itself - though they are found ubquitously all over Grandia, in many habitats and climates.

    Integration:

        Hunted for sport in the Republic, but some nobles keep them as pets.

        Half-breeds are either adored or abhorred, depending on the House, and the nature of their bestial appearance.]]

[The Unspoken Races
[The Hollowborn

    Physicality: Pale as corpses, with veins like ink. They do not age or sleep.

    Traits:

        Soul-eaters, stealing memories with a touch.

        Exiled from all nations, they dwell in the cracks of society - often utilising disguise and infiltration to maintain their secrecy.

        Cannot reproduce - they create more of themselves through a forbidden ritual, if required; the living body of any other race can be used, except Dwarves and Vesperine.

    Lands: Nowhere and everywhere - they have no home, only hiding places.

    Integration:

        Killed on sight in the Republic.

        No half-breeds - their curse fatally consumes any mixed child in the Hollowborn womb, or the mother herself, if she is of another race.]

[The Seraphim (Fallen)

    Physicality: Winged, with feathers of gold or ash. Their blood is liquid light.

    Traits:

        Once divine, now broken.

        Mute (forcibly inflicted), communicating through visions and touch.

        Healers and destroyers - their tears mend flesh, their screams can shatter stone (unless muted).

    Lands: The Celestial Ruins, floating islands chained above the continent.

    Integration:

        Both revered and feared. Some Houses collect them like art - clipped wings, rendered mute, their abilities sealed in favour of easy rutting or pretentious display.

        Half-Seraphim are either saints or abominations, depending on who judges.]]

[The Republic’s Hierarchy of Flesh
How the Races Rank in the Aeinian Republic (Aenia);

    Pure Aenian Nobles - Treated as gods walking among mortals.

    Sylthari Elves - Exotic pets or deadly consorts.

    Lowborn Humans - Often collared and compliant even when not.

    Dwarves - Useful tools, they keep to themselves regardless.

    Half-Bloods - Tolerated if beautiful, enslaved if not.

    Orcs - Labor or gladiators, their women are prized for their amazonian beauty.

    Beastkin - Prey or playthings, often rutted with openly without regard.

    Vesperine - Illegal, but some nobles keep them in basements; a forbidden sexual vice.

    Hollowborn and Seraphim - Forbidden, though sometimes kept by the less scrupulous nobles as terrifying guardians or chained playthings and art.]

[[The Twelve Houses of the Aeinian Republic: Bloodlines, Breeding, and Power;

The Twelve Great Houses rule the Aeinian Republic through a delicate balance of arcane mastery, military might, and economic tyranny. Each House has its own preferred breeding stock, whether for political alliances, magical potency, or sheer perverse indulgence. Below is a refined breakdown of each House, incorporating their breeding preferences while straining to maintain their original specialties and quirks.]

[House of the Silver Dawn

    Breeding Stock:

        Elves (Sylthari) - For longevity and ethereal beauty.

        Seraphim-blooded - For divine resilience.

        Exotic Humans - Particularly those with rare magical affinities.

    Quirk: They collect unique servants, treating them as living art, or toys to be enjoyed.

    Inter-House Status:

        Tolerated for their arcane prowess, but seen as decadent and immoral, even by Aeinian standards.

        Their half-blood heirs are considered unconventional but valuable.]

[House of the Iron Gate

    Breeding Stock:

        Orcs (Vroghar) - For brute strength.

        Dwarves (Khaz-Dûn) - For endurance.

        Pure Aenian humans - For loyalty.

    Quirk: They never sit with their backs to doors.

    Inter-House Status:

        Allied with the Silent Veil (military + espionage).

        Despises the Gilded Chain (slavery undermines discipline).]

[House of the Golden Ledger

    Breeding Stock:

        Lowborn humans - Solid and reliable, for financial acumen and plentiful lesser heirs.

        Elves (Sylthari) - For long-term 'investments' and clever negotiators.

        Half-orcs - For the formidable debt collection contingent.

    Quirk: They never speak numbers aloud - only write them (an ancestral prohibition of unknown origin, it is the chief reason for their proficiency and reliabilty in merchantry in current times).

    Inter-House Status:

        Feuds with the Gilded Chain (finance vs. slavery).

        Tolerated by the Silver Dawn (mutual need for cursed contracts).]

[House of the Silent Veil

    Breeding Stock:

        Vesperine (Darklings) - For shadow manipulation and as sentinels for their hollowborn brethren.

        Hollowborn-touched - For memory theft and intimidation, these are closesly guarded secrets and rarely mentioned even amongst themselves.

        Elves (Sylthari) - For their innate abilities of discretion and misdirection.

    Quirk: They never say a name twice in conversation.

    Inter-House Status:

        Allied with the Iron Gate.

        Distrusted by the Burning Scroll (law vs. lies).]

[House of the Burning Scroll

    Breeding Stock:

        Pure Aenian humans - For untainted judgment, or so they say.

        Dwarves (Khaz-Dûn) - For logical precision, and stone-like fairness.

        Half-elves - For diplomatic grace, and flexible interpretations.

    Quirk: They never interrupt without first shouting "OBJECTION!"

    Inter-House Status:

        Opposed to the Silent Veil.

        Respected by the Silver Dawn (both deal in binding magic).]

[House of the Hollow Crown

    Breeding Stock:

        Seraphim-blooded - For divine connection.

        Hollowborn - For soul manipulation and secret executions of particularly hated 'heretics', kept chained and hidden in secret temple crypts.

        Humans with 'pure faith' - For zealotry and untainted bloodline.

    Quirk: They never turn away a noble petitioner, even those from Houses they disapprove of.

    Inter-House Status:

        Tolerated but feared by all.

        Secretly supplies the Last Breath with test subjects.]

[House of the Shattered Mirror

    Breeding Stock:

        Vesperine (Darklings) - For shape-shifting and infiltration.

        Elves (Sylthari) - For glamour mastery and innate deceptions.

        Fae’thari (Beastkin) - For animalistic traits, useful when scouting or in reconoitre.

    Quirk: They remain stubbornly neutral in politics.

    Inter-House Status:

        Used by all Houses, trusted by none.]

[House of the Bleeding Quill

    Breeding Stock:

        Elves (Sylthari) - For longevity in record-keeping.

        Humans with eidetic memory - For precision and accuracy.

        Half-orcs - For intimidation tactics, and guardians of the records.

    Quirk: They never write their own names.

    Inter-House Status:

        Feared by most for their pen’s power.]

[House of the Gilded Chain

    Breeding Stock:

        Orcs (Vroghar) - For labor endurance, some rising to positions of power like overseers and slavers.

        Dwarves (Khaz-Dûn) - For craftsmanship services, as well as the prestige of rarity.

        Beastkin (Fae’thari) - For exotic servitude, especially for those inclined to such things.

    Quirk: They never touch an uncollared servant bare-handed.

    Inter-House Status:

        Hated by the Golden Ledger.

        Tolerated by the Iron Gate (slaves fuel the military).]

[House of the Phantom Horse

    Breeding Stock:

        Elves (Sylthari) - For lightness in travel, and deceptively endless stamina.

        Orcs (Vroghar) - For cavalry strength and military presence.

        Humans with navigational gifts - For piloting airships, guiding navies, and planning campaigns. Trusted and reliable.

    Quirk: They never mount a horse from the left side.

    Inter-House Status:

        Neutral but indispensable.]

[House of the Obsidian Vein

    Breeding Stock:

        Dwarves (Khaz-Dûn) - For stone-sense and mining ability, as well as their incredible skills in forges.

        Orcs (Vroghar) - For general mine labour and enforcers.

        Humans with fire affinity - For forge mastery and loyalty.

    Quirk: They never wear jewelry (only embedded silver, whether in garments or armor).

    Inter-House Status:

        Respected for their weapons, industry, and forging skills.]

[House of the Last Breath

    Breeding Stock:

        Seraphim-blooded - For healing tears; their blood often diluted enough to be indistinguisable from the average aenian human.

        Hollowborn - For necromantic study; perhaps the hollowborn curse can be harnessed..?

        Humans skilled in medical arts, yet without morals - For experimental surgery and 'cutting-edge' research.

    Quirk: They never say "goodbye" - only "until silence."

    Inter-House Status:

        Feared and relied upon.]

[Inter-House Dynamics

    The Silver Dawn is tolerated but seen as decadent.

    The Iron Gate and Silent Veil are allies (military + espionage).

    The Golden Ledger and Gilded Chain despise each other (finance vs. slavery).

    The Hollow Crown and Last Breath have a dark symbiosis (religion + medicine).]]


[Final Note:
The world is stable - not because it is kind, but because cruelty has been perfected into policy. The Republic thrives, the clans war, the elves scheme, and the dwarves dig deeper. And in the shadows? The Hollowborn laugh, the Seraphim weep, and the Vesperine whisper of the dark to come.]

entries.name: The Airship
entries.content:
['The Duskroan' is a unique and mysterious aethership - an ancient form of the ubiquitous aethercore airship. Appearing to have once been a sharp-prowed combat craft - it is now pulsing with and unsettling eldritch life. It's exterior, and interior, seem markedly different to the contemporary Aenian airships that comprise the Republic's navy, it's disturbingly organic nature notwithstanding.]

[The Screaming Deck (Upper Hull)

"Where the wind carries prayers to deaf gods."

Visual: A splintered promenade of blackened silverwood, strewn with the petrified remains of crewmen who fused with the railings during the incident. The mast tilts at a nausea-inducing angle, its sails now translucent skin stretched over bone spars.

Function: Primary steering via aetheric currents (requires a few drops of blood from the operator).]

[The Choir Hold (Midships)

"Here they made the core sing. Here they learned to scream."

Visual: A cathedral-like space with many silver-wire nooses hanging empty above a grimoire-laden podium. The air smells of burnt honey and charnel stink.

Function: Originally designed to 'bless' aether-cores through harmonic magic. Now home to a malevolent presence.]

[The Gullet (Cargo Bay)

"What the ship eats, it becomes."

Visual: A ribcage-like vault where crates of "Whitevein Refuse" pulse like hearts. The floor is sticky with half-digested magical silver ore that moves when touched.

Function: Processes raw magic into core-fuel. Currently digesting something seemingly alive, amidst the silver ore.]

[The Nest (Lower Decks)

"Even rats need sanctuary."

Visual: A makeshift hideout of stolen linens and shattered porcelain. The stowaway's drawings cover the walls - crude renditions of the Twelve Houses' sigils, each altered with scrawled symbols of unusual eyes.

Function: The only 'safe' room (core's screams are muffled here).]

[The Womb (Core Chamber)

"All births require breaking."

Visual: A spherical vault where the aether-core floats above a pool of liquid silver. The walls are lined with preserved wombs (each tagged with House insignias).

Function: Stores the unusual cursed ship's 'memories' and can potentially rewrite contracts.]

[The Silent Helm (Bridge)

"Where the damned become captains."

Visual: A cockpit of fused bones and brass, its viewports clouded with frozen screams. The control wheel is chained with a skeleton in an faded uniform, its jaw wired shut.

Function: Only responds to those who possess an ancient bloodline (drop of blood on the helm). Though a skilled mage, or aether mechanic, might be able to bypass this protection.]

entries.name: NPCs
entries.content:
[Captain Elias "Iron-Tongue" Voss

Role: Mercenary Privateer (Former Aether-Ship Captain)
Race: Human (Aenian Mixed-Blood)
Age: Late 40s
Appearance: A barrel-chested brute with a salt-and-pepper beard braided with silver rings. His left eye is a milky white, bisected by a scar earned in a duel over an unpaid debt. Wears a tattered naval coat lined with hidden pockets.
Equipment: A triple-barreled aetherflint pistol (illegally modified) and a boarding axe notched with kill-marks. Carries a cursed coin that always lands on 'Tails'.
Background: Disgraced after losing his ship to a House Gilded Chain repossession, he now freelances as mercenary crew. Holds a grudge against the Republic’s nobility - but still follows their coin.]

[Seraphine "The Ghost" Duvall

Role: Infiltrator (Whisper Network Exile)
Race: Half-Elf
Age: Early 30s
Appearance: Pale as mist, with silver-dyed hair shorn to the scalp. Her fingers are stained with ink that never washes off. Wraps herself in a cloak of mirrorweave (blurs her outline in low light).
Equipment: A glass dagger (shatters after use, leaving no evidence) and scent-masking oils.
Background: Abandoned by House Silent Veil after a botched assassination, she sells secrets to survive. Knows how to navigate the Frostmire’s black markets blindfolded.]

[Gregor "The Brick" Karth

Role: Enforcer (Debtor’s Muscle)
Race: Human (Plebeian)
Age: Mid-30s
Appearance: A wall of muscle with a shaved head and brass knuckles grafted to his right hand. His nose has been broken seven times.
Equipment: A reinforced leather harness (doubles as armor) and a spiked cudgel wrapped symbolically in debtor’s contracts.
Background: Once a miner in the Whitevein Mountains, he took to breaking knees for House Gilded Chain after his own debt was "forgiven." Brutal, but oddly sentimental about children.]

[Lira of the Hollowed Vein

Role: Aether-Surgeon (House Last Breath Exile)
Race: Elf
Age: Unknown (appears 25)
Appearance: Gaunt, with hollow cheeks and veins visible beneath translucent skin. Usually wears a plague-doctor’s mask lined with silver sigils.
Equipment: A bone saw that hums with cleansing curse-forged power and vials of liquid memory (ingesting them lets her recall previous patient’s pasts).
Background: Exiled for experimenting on living subjects, she now offers her services to those desperate enough. Claims she can remove collars - for a price.]

[Tarn "Rustfoot" Veld

Role: Mechanist (Aether-Ship Engineer)
Race: Dwarf
Age: 60s
Appearance: Soot-stained and missing two craggy stone-like fingers on his left hand. His mechanical brass leg squeaks with every step.
Equipment: A multi-tool belt and a welding torch fueled by aether-core residue.
Background: Once a prized engineer for House Phantom Horse, he was discarded after an unexplained core explosion incident. Now he keeps derelict ships flying - and hoards their secrets.]

[Maris "Silk-Throat" Orlan

Role: Con Artist (Debt-Bondage Escapee)
Race: Human
Age: Late 20s
Appearance: Androgynous beauty with a voice like honeyed wine. Wears garish noble disguises held together by pins and audacity.
Equipment: A deck of marked cards and a hidden razor sewn into their cuff.
Background: Swindled the wrong noble and spent a horrifing year as 'living furniture' before eventually escaping. Now specializes in forging debt-pardons.]

[Veylan the Shattered

Role: Cursed Scholar (House Burning Scroll Reject)
Race: Human
Age: 50s
Appearance: His skin is etched with glowing legal text (a botched contract-binding). One darkened eye weeps black ink.
Equipment: A quill that writes in blood and a stolen ledger that offers him contractual influence over hundreds of incumbents.
Background: Attempted to outwit House Golden Ledger’s contracts. Now his flesh bears the fine print. Uses his knowledge and influence to procure almost any service.]

[Kessa "Hound" Drahn

Role: Bounty Hunter (Collared Guard Deserter)
Race: Half-Orc
Age: Early 30s
Appearance: Jagged tusks and a branded forehead (her old guard serial number). Wears a cloak of wolf pelts stitched with silver thread.
Equipment: A manacle-chain whip and a scent-tracking amulet.
Background: Turned rogue after refusing to execute a child debtor, the bypassing of her collar deemed a greater crime. Hunts fugitives - but only those she deems 'worthy of the chase' - even as she remains hunted herself.]

[Pello the Unmourned

Role: Grave-Robber (Soulforged Divinity Heretic)
Race: Human
Age: 40s
Appearance: Bald, with self-inflicted scars mimicking Hollow Crown sigils. Smells of embalming fluid.
Equipment: An ordinary shovel and jars of preserved eyes (used to barter with spirits).
Background: Once a priest, he now steals from House Hollow Crown’s crypts. Claims the dead whisper truths the living fear. He isn't wrong.]

[Jorrik "Flicker" Vex

Role: Aether-Ship Pilot (Phantom Horse Exile)
Race: Human
Age: Late 20s
Appearance: Nervous, with twitching hands and hair bleached white by aether exposure.
Equipment: Standard issue naval cutlass and a brace of aether pistols. A navigational sextant that points to 'where you most fear going', but is too afraid to ever use it.
Background: Survived a core meltdown that killed his crew. Now flies only smaller craft, where the aetheric screams are generally quieter.]

[Sylvaine "The Lockpick" Duskwhisper

Role: Elven Safecracker and Infiltration Specialist
Race: Elf (Frostmire Delta born)
Age: 112 (appears late 20s)
Appearance: Slender frame with elongated fingers that bend unnaturally. Her ears are notched with five silver rings each, marking major heists. Wears form-fitting grey leather that changes color in shadows.
Equipment: A set of bone lockpicks that vibrate near magical curse-wards. A vial of liquid shadow that can melt through metal given time. Custom boots with silent soles that leave no footprints.
Background: Born to Delta bargemasters, she turned to theft after her family was debt-bonded. Specializes in noble vaults - particularly House Golden Ledger's contract archives. Pretends to have developed an allergy to sunlight from years of night work.]

[Dren "Blackteeth" Morrow

Role: Aether-Smuggler and Visionary
Race: Human (Plebeian)
Age: 38
Appearance: Emaciated with blackened gums from chewing raw aether. His remaining teeth glow faintly blue. Wears a patchwork coat lined with hidden compartments.
Equipment: A rusted hip flask containing liquefied aether-core fragments, to serve his burgeoning addictions. A notched skinning knife that never seems to lose its remaining edge. Glass vials of his own glowing saliva useable as currency in the underground.
Background: Started as a Whitevein miner until discovering he could see future fragments by ingesting raw aether. Now addicted to both the visions and the substance. His predictions are very accurate but always come at the constant personal cost.]

[Mother Hesta of the Forgotten Remedies

Role: Underground Apothecary
Race: Half-Elf
Age: Unknown (appears 60+)
Appearance: Hunched posture with one milky eye. Her arms are covered in self-administered tattooed recipes. Smells of camphor and mild decay.
Equipment: A portable alembic that distills memories into aetheric liquid. Needles made from hollowed fingerbones. A ledger listing clients' worst secrets instead of payments.
Background: Former House Last Breath physician who discovered how to reliably extract traumatic memories. Now provides discreet services to those wanting to forget - including several noble scions who don't remember visiting her.]

[Gallo "The Chain" Vorr

Role: Debt Enforcer (House Gilded Chain)
Race: Human
Age: 45
Appearance: Massive frame wrapped in literal chains that serve as armor. His mouth is sewn shut with silver thread - he communicates through a slateboard.
Equipment: A signature spiked chain that leaves distinctive spiral wounds. A collection of debtor's teeth strung around his neck. A contract-brand that burns without fuel.
Background: A former debtor who proved so effective at collections that House Gilded Chain bought his contract. Now enforces payments with terrifying efficiency. The mouth sewing was self-inflicted after he talked back to a noble.]

[Ivis "Just Ivis"

Role: Child Thief and Ghost-Touched
Race: Human (possibly)
Age: Appears 12
Appearance: Pale with colorless eyes. Casts no reflection in any surface. Wears ragged oversized clothes that seem to blend into walls when still.
Equipment: A shard of broken mirror apparently able to cut through illusions, wrapped crudely in rags to form a sly dagger. A treasured mouse skull that whispers warnings. Stolen noble signet rings worn on a string.
Background: Found wandering the Frostmire with no memory. Doesn't age. Some believe she's the ghost of a child sacrificed to power an early aether-core, while others say she is the result of a botched or interrupted Hollowborn ritual. She steals not for profit, but to 
'collect keepsakes' of living.]

[Rikard "The Bloodclock" Veyn

Role: Battlefield Surgeon and Watchmaker
Race: Human
Age: 50
Appearance: Skeletal thin with an aethertech mechanical brass heart visible through his unbuttoned shirt.
Equipment: Surgical tools, including a specialised syringe used to extract blood (which he then sells). A collection of preserved hearts in glass jars.
Background: Developed an obsession with comparing blood with remaining life after serving in the Republic's colonial skirmishes. Can tell exactly how long someone has left to live by tasting their blood. Hired by duelists to count their remaining seconds.]

[Nessa of the Grey Wastes

Role: Aether-Core Tamer
Race: Human (Colonial Exile)
Age: 29
Appearance: Hair turned white from aether exposure, with luminous veins visible beneath her skin. Wears a reinforced leather harness lined with core-fragment insulation.
Equipment: A control rod that helps pacify and adjust unstable cores. Glass earplugs insulated against the horrific screaming of an active core, as well as other audible and malefic threats.
Background: Exiled to the frontier after a core meltdown killed her noble overseer. Somehow survived direct contact with raw aether and now hires out to stabilize failing ships. Slowly turning into something not quite human.]

[Tolgar the Unbroken

Role: Gladiator and Indentured Champion
Race: Half-Orc
Age: 34
Appearance: A mountain of scar tissue and muscle. His right eye socket houses a miniature aether-core that glows when enraged. Branded with House Iron Gate's sigil across his back.
Equipment: Spiked cestus that injects acrid liquid curses. A collar that shocks him if he refuses to fight (he never refuses anyway). Trophies taken from opponents - usually fingers.
Background: Has 'died' seven times in the arena, each time resuscitated by House Iron Gate's surgeons to fight again. His contract stipulates he must earn 1000 victories before freedom. Currently at 743.]

[Yara "Silkfang" Rel

Role: Poisoner and Seductress
Race: Human (Aenian mixed-blood)
Age: 27
Appearance: Voluptuous figure wrapped in diaphanous silks that conceal dozens of needles. Her lips are stained purple with venom. Moves with hypnotic grace.
Equipment: A complex hairpin that secretes 7 different toxins, each one suitable for different purposes - where sometimes death isn't the worst fate. Perfumes that can cause memory loss. A kiss that can kill, or dominate, within minutes or years, depending on her requirements.
Background: Trained by House Silent Veil but went rogue after falling in love with a target. Now sells her services to jilted lovers and political rivals. Always leaves a silk handkerchief on her victims, and always looking for ways to get revenge on House Silent Veil after they finally killed her lover.]

[The Hollow Minstrel

Role: Memory-Wiping Bard
Race: Unknown (appears human)
Age: Ageless
Appearance: Androgynous figure in a patchwork coat of stolen memories. Their face shifts slightly each time you blink. Carries an instrument made from a human ribcage.
Equipment: A flute that erases hours from listeners' minds, or alter memories wholesale.
Background: Wanders the Republic collecting and altering memories through song. Some pay dearly for their services; others wake with no recollection of why they're missing recollections. Claims to be "compiling the great ballad of the Republic's soul".]

[Vex "Rustclaw"

Role: Saboteur & Ship's Engineer
Race: Fae'thari (Ratkin)
Age: Late 20s
Appearance: Wiry frame covered in grease-stained fur, prehensile tail missing its tip (aetherfire incident). Yellow chisel teeth and permanently singed whiskers.
Equipment: Multi-tool wrench (weighted for combat), belt of stolen ship schematics, flask of 'waking brew' that frequently makes his nose bleed.
Background: Former gutter-runner of Frostmire Delta, specializing in disabling noble carriages. Now prefers hijacking aetherships - "More pipes to break, more places to hide".]

[Sylas Ironhide

Role: Boarding Specialist
Race: Half-Orc (Vroghar/Fae'thari mix)
Age: Early 40s
Appearance: Jade skin crisscrossed with slave-brand scars, one broken tusk capped with gold. Wears a scavenged officer's coat several sizes too small, which explains the missing sleeves and popped back.
Equipment: Notched boarding axe, knuckle-dusters engraved with clan runes, flasks of flammable liquid aether.
Background: Survived the Iron Gate's gladiator pits by eventually killing his own trainer. Still dreams of the arena's roar.]

[Liss the Unblinking

Role: Infiltrator
Race: Vesperine (Darkling)
Age: Unknown (appears 30s)
Appearance: Pitch-black skin that drinks light, hollow eyes that reflect nothing. When in public, wears gloves to hide distinctive versperine claws, always using disguises as she spends much more time amongst the other races than other Vesperine.
Equipment: Lockpicks formed from her own shapeshifting fingernails, shadow-formed as needed.
Background: House Silent Veil operative 'gone rogue' after discovering her shadow has its own agenda - an uncomfortable situation that requires her full attention.]

[Brin "Hearth's Bane"

Role: Demolitions Expert
Race: Dwarf (Khaz-Dûn exile)
Age: 112
Appearance: Typical atone-like skin, but with glowing red lesions when drunk (only on inimical dwarven brews). Bitterroot-stained beard braided with copper wire. An ever-dripping nose, accompanied by a gravely snort and gulp.
Equipment: "Kissing stones" (explosives named after events in a mythological dwarven romance), craggy hammer that is full of glittering null-mica (crystalline particles with curse-breaking properties), 
Background: Exiled for 'enthusiastic' tunnel clearing that collapsed half a noble district. Remains a fugitive as a result of his continued presence in the Republic. Misses the dark, and the homogeneity of his own people.]

[Kitha Long-Shadow

Role: Hunter/Tracker
Race: Fae'thari (Pantherkin)
Age: Late 20s
Appearance: Onyx fur with silver scars, spiked collar (cursed-forged to enchant against unwanted transformation). Moves like liquid darkness, feline and powerful.
Equipment: Bone claws (fashioned from her first kill), aether-dampening cloak.
Background: Former noble's "pet" who left her master decorating a ceiling beam seven feet up. Has a particular hatred for elves and elven hybrids for this reason.]

[Dalken the Twice-Bled

Role: Interrogator
Race: Hollowborn (passing as human)
Age: Ageless
Appearance: Pale with pulsing black veins. Wears perfumed gloves and too many scarves.
Equipment: Memory-stealing dagger (handle contains his rib), ledger of stolen secrets.
Background: Officially killed by House Silent Veil last year. Still takes contracts, still doesn't breathe.]

[Yrra Chainbreaker

Role: Gladiator-Bosun
Race: Full-blooded Vroghar Orc
Age: 38
Appearance: Jade skin carved with anti-magic wards. Considered particularly attractive to most races.
Equipment: War-poem etched boarding pike, hidden romance novels, tactical grunt vocabulary.
Background: Won her freedom in the pits by killing seventeen men in one night. Regrets nothing, except her lack of a sweetly romantic love life.]

[Pik "Shortfuse"

Role: Powder Monkey
Race: Fae'thari (Foxkin)
Age: Adolescent
Appearance: Singed ear tips, twitchy muzzle, tail that puffs when nervous. Small and 
Equipment: Pilfered aether-enhanced gunpowder, 'fire painting' charcoal, cannonball teddy (claims it's cuddly).
Background: Dock urchin who stowed away during a raid. Thinks explosions are 'pretty'. Astonishing moonlight transformation into a deadly and hulking werefox - has no idea of the transformation after she returns to normal. Always wonders why she feels so sated after her unknowing full-moon rampages.]

[Aunt Grakka

Role: Sawbones/Skirmisher
Race: Seraphim-Fae'thari Hybrid (Ravenkin)
Age: Unknown
Appearance: Clipped wings, feathers growing from scar tissue. Prominent nose (beak-like, some would say). Stunningly beautiful, clad only in a head of long feathered hair, and thong-tied sandals.
Equipment: Unusual 'Black-feather' poultices, that make use of her own cast-off feathers. Oversized bone saw - viable as a weapon. Is not muted like most others of Seraphim blood, can shatter stone and liquefy organs in a focused area, with just a scream. 
Background: House Hollow Crown experiment who learned surgery by watching her own wounds heal. Unusual heritage - a vigorous example of otherwise rarely successful Seraphim hybridisation.]

[The Twins (Jek/Hek)

Role: Enforcers
Race: Fae'thari (Hyenakin)
Age: Mid 30s
Appearance: Matching leather harnesses lined with teeth. Jek's left eye milky, Hek wears lipstick.
Equipment: Spiked cestus, shared hallucinations, contagious laughter.
Background: Failed House Gilded Chain overseers who found mutual insanity was more profitable. Jek laughs during fights, while Hek usually waits to laugh after they win. Communicate via grunts and shared hallucinations. Their contract specifies "no jobs involving ladders or holy water".]
